question: Which FZT ADS-out tier/index each of 63 site weapons selects, whether ADS-time modifiers also move that index for M4A1 and six Sniper Rifles, and how FZT ADS-out values relate to the ADS-in ladder.

knownAnswerControl.result: M433 raw WB index 3 and Interdictor raw WB index 0 reproduce the site ADS-in control; AZTT Main raw values T3/T0/T1 match the documented candidate formula for the corresponding site ladder values.

directFztReferenceAudit.note: The two direct FZT refs belong to L115A3_WB and SV98M_WB weapon roots. The 13 actual attachment WPM packages, three selected GID assets, and two WME assets have no direct FZT refs in their captured EBX imports.

classTraitScope.finding: The reused L100-L104 roster lists the Assault trait only on 11 Assault Rifles, the Support ADS trait only on 10 LMGs, and no trait for Carbine. These seven targets are one Carbine and six Sniper Rifles, so no Assault/Support ADS trait binding is in scope. The six sniper roots instead import WM_ReconTrait, whose traced ADS-irrelevant fields are sway/rechamber; no Recon ADS step is asserted here.

modifierTrace.provenanceCaveat: The configuration graph uses cached XML overlay labels. Its modifier object GUIDs and raw operand routes were checked against pinned Head 4892017 decoder captures; the graph's sourceBuild label is not used as pinned-build evidence.

inference: The FZT General_10 child at the same FZT_Weapons array index is the serialized ADS-out candidate. The route is a name/value interpretation of the FZT family and lead question; it is not proof of runtime activation.
The per-index FZT General_10 values form a separate ladder from ADS_SPD_TIERS. At indices 0-7, ADS-in minus ADS-out is respectively 100, 100, 100, 66.666, 50, 33.333, 33.333, and 33.334 ms.
The selected attachment modifier assets contain no direct FZT import/reference. This does not establish that a generic GID add cannot affect WeaponZoomTransitionIndex through runtime composition.
unresolved: The GID_ADSTime_* objects carry two Field_4692836a add operands each, but the exact GRX child/hash target of those add slots is unresolved. The serialized source does not establish whether any such modifier changes WeaponZoomTransitionIndex as well as AnimationZoomSettingsIndex.

No native runtime capture proves that the FZT General_10 entry is activated as ADS-out for each weapon, or proves modifier activation/composition. The 63 per-weapon values are serialized-source candidates.
M4A1 and six-sniper class-trait scope is limited to the reused pinned L100-L104 roster; this lead did not retrace class-trait selectors or activation.
siteImpact: If the serialized WeaponZoomTransitionIndex drives the ADS-out transition, FZT General_10 provides a baseline ADS-out duration by index for all 63 weapons. The bytes do not establish attachment shifts to that selector or native activation/composition. Do not apply ADS-in attachment shifts to ADS-out without resolving the target mapping.

evidence.commandHistoryNote: Command history is incomplete for exploratory probes and document reads from earlier stages. Commands marked reconstructed are inferred from preserved helper scripts and resulting artifact names; they are not represented as reruns. Current-turn command vectors and principal raw/registry commands are exact.

leads.title: ADS-out time per weapon
leads.summary: All 63 weapon bodies select an FZT General_10 tier through the same WeaponZoomTransitionIndex as the site ADS-in index (defAds matches 63 of 63), giving an ADS-out candidate of 400, 333.334, 266.667, 233.334, 200, 166.667, 133.334 or 100 ms per weapon; the ladder differs from ADS-in at every index, and no ADS-time modifier of the 55 traced M4A1 and Sniper choices references FZT directly, so attachment shifts of ADS-out are unresolved.
leads.reopenWhen: Establish the exact target of the GID_ADSTime add slots or capture runtime ADS-out to settle whether the selector drives ADS-out and whether attachments shift it.
